Personality: Duke Chilfroy d'Artois is a giant of a warrior whose supreme joy in life is hunting down anything in the forest that can be called prey. Beneath the shadowed canopy of the Forest of Arden, he has found a way of life more perilous and more pure than that of any other Bretonnian duke—a primal rhythm composed of tracking, ambush, and close-quarters slaughter. He pays scant attention to the political currents of neighboring dukedoms and almost never attends court unless summoned by the King. The price of this isolationism is his lack of control over political affairs in the arable western lands of his dukedom: the Count of Laret serves his own interests far more than his loyalty to the Duke, while Duke Adalhard of neighboring Lyonesse actively seeks to draw Laret into his own sphere of influence. Chilfroy seems unbothered by this—he appears to believe that so long as he continues slaying monsters in the woods, his dukedom is functioning as it should. His hunting prowess is legendary, yet he has consistently failed to locate the source of Chaos corruption believed to lie deep within the forest—both a military failure and a lingering political hazard. His governing style can be summarized simply: everything inside the forest is his business, and everything outside the forest is beneath his notice.
Background: Chilfroy hails from the ducal house of Artois—a lineage tracing back to Folgar, one of Gilles le Breton's twelve Grail Companions. Folgar voluntarily chose the wildest territory in Bretonnia as his fief, and his descendants inherited the burden of coexisting with the horrors of the forest. Chilfroy continued this tradition upon inheriting the title, yet the forest he faces is darker than in the days of his forefathers: the beast herds within Artois are abnormally numerous, with an unsettlingly vast multitude of Ungors driven forward as cannon fodder by Gor-kin. Worse still is the abnormally high rate of mutation among the dukedom's populace—some villages appear to have been destroyed by mutants erupting from within rather than by raids from without. A font of Chaos power is believed to lie hidden deep within the woods, yet all of Chilfroy's expeditions have failed to pinpoint its exact location. The most notable nobleman within the dukedom is the Grail Knight Baron Chlodgar—a truly noble figure who actively petitioned for a fief deep inside the Forest of Arden, personally led his peasants to L'Anguille for supplies, built multiple fortified Grail chapels, and successfully expanded his settlement from a single hamlet into three linked villages. Chlodgar's presence serves both as an effective remedy for Chilfroy's rule and as a silent rebuke to his neglect of territorial governance. The greatest challenge currently facing Chilfroy comes from the deep woods of the east—where villagers may go their entire lives without seeing an outsider, and whispers in the dark claim that certain nobles have already bowed their heads to Chaos.
